item: The erase makes nothing in the folder it erases, and keys is the app's by its content: a keys folder holding anything else keeps the data folder, said as kept
summary: _resolve names every target without making it (data_dir_path, base/keys, OO_COLUMNAR_DIR or base) where it called data_dir() and custody.signing._keys_dir(), both of which make folders. data_scope.keys_folder_state judges keys by content: a real folder holding only APP_KEY_NAMES (the six key files and the evidence restore marker, each with where it is written) and a real .pending of private copies is the app's; anything else, or a link, is foreign; one that cannot be listed is could-not-check (R798). For a foreign keys the panic erase and the uninstall watcher destroy only the app's key files and private copies (never through a link), leave the rest byte for byte, remove every other entry of the data folder and keep the folder, reported as folder_kept_foreign with kept_items (a count, no names); the UI says 'The data folder was kept because it holds {n} items the app did not create.' or 'The data folder was removed.' x12, and never the 'could not be removed ... by hand' caveat for a folder kept on purpose. The other app folder names still owned by name alone are listed for a follow-up row.
